source.title: Human Atlas selected archaeological contexts
source.license: Original editorial selection; linked sources retain their own terms
source.note: Each row is a named evidence context with a broad display window. It is not a culture polygon, demographic estimate, language map, ancestry model, or route.

records.name: Progress 2 burial complex
records.note: Selected North Caucasus burial context used in ancient-DNA and archaeological discussion of steppe communities. The convention is archaeological; it does not name a people or a migration path.
records.sourceTitle: Wang et al. 2019 · Ancient human genome-wide data from a 3000-year interval in the Caucasus

records.name: Kalmykia Catacomb burial context
records.note: Reference point for a Catacomb-period funerary context in the lower Volga steppe. Its window is a broad archaeological display range, not continuous cemetery use.
records.sourceTitle: Mallory and Adams · Encyclopedia of Indo-European Culture, Catacomb Grave Culture

records.name: Sintashta fortified settlement and cemetery
records.note: Fortified settlement and associated cemetery evidence near the upper Tobol. The label names an archaeological convention, not an ethnic or linguistic identity.
records.sourceTitle: Epimakhov · The Sintashta Culture and the Indo-Iranian Problem

records.name: Arkaim fortified settlement
records.note: A fortified settlement in the southern Urals. It is shown as a settlement-phase context alongside, not as proof of, regional movement.
records.sourceTitle: Russian Academy of Sciences · Arkaim archaeological reserve

records.name: Frattesina
records.note: Late Bronze Age production and exchange settlement context in the Po plain. The Urnfield label is a material-culture convention, not a population category.
records.sourceTitle: Bietti Sestieri · The Bronze Age in Europe

records.name: Hallstatt salt mine
records.association: Commonly discussed in relation to early Celtic-language contexts; this is not proof that a single language or people occupied the site
records.note: Salt-mining and cemetery context at Hallstatt. Hallstatt is an archaeological convention based on material culture and chronology.
records.sourceTitle: Hallstatt Museum · Archaeology and salt mining

records.name: La Tene lakeshore site
records.association: Commonly discussed in relation to later Celtic-language contexts; the association does not map an ethnicity, territory, or language boundary
records.note: The type-site context for the La Tene archaeological convention. Finds and deposition history do not define a people or an area of control.

records.name: Wielbark cemetery area near Malbork
records.association: Later written sources discuss Goths in parts of this wider region; Wielbark material culture is not itself a Goth identity map
records.note: Reference cemetery area for the Wielbark archaeological convention. It is kept distinct from later ethnonyms and political histories.
records.sourceTitle: Encyclopaedia of the Archaeology of Ancient History · Wielbark culture overview

records.name: Mycenae
records.note: Palatial, settlement, and funerary evidence at Mycenae. The label identifies a material and chronological convention, not a uniform political or social order.
records.sourceTitle: UNESCO · Archaeological Sites of Mycenae and Tiryns

records.name: Tiryns
records.note: Fortified settlement context within the Mycenaean chronological horizon. It is shown as a place with evidence, not as a route endpoint.
records.sourceTitle: UNESCO · Archaeological Sites of Mycenae and Tiryns

records.name: Tyre
records.note: Urban and maritime settlement context. Phoenician is used here as a historical and archaeological descriptor, not a homogeneous population identity.

records.name: Carthage
records.note: Urban context conventionally described as Punic. This point does not trace maritime expansion or delimit a cultural territory.

records.name: Cerveteri necropolis
records.note: Necropolis evidence at Cerveteri. Etruscan is a conventional historical and archaeological descriptor; the point does not define an Etruscan boundary.
records.sourceTitle: UNESCO · Etruscan Necropolises of Cerveteri and Tarquinia

records.name: Tarquinia necropolis
records.note: Necropolis evidence at Tarquinia, displayed separately from political and linguistic reconstructions.
records.sourceTitle: UNESCO · Etruscan Necropolises of Cerveteri and Tarquinia

records.name: Pompeii
records.note: Urban settlement evidence with an exceptionally visible terminal event. The selected window is not the whole occupational history of the site.
records.sourceTitle: UNESCO · Archaeological Areas of Pompei, Herculaneum and Torre Annunziata
